Main.sentence: Arctic Alaska or Far North Alaska is a ___E:region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Region)___ of the ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ ___E:state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state)___ of ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ generally referring to the northern areas on or close to the ___E:Arctic Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_Ocean)___ .

It commonly includes ___E:North Slope Borough U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Slope_Borough,_Alaska)___ , ___E:Northwest Arctic Borough U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Arctic_Borough,_Alaska)___ , ___E:Nome Census Area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nome_Census_Area,_Alaska)___ , and is sometimes taken to include parts of the ___E:Yukon-Koyukuk Census Area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yukon-Koyukuk_Census_Area,_Alaska)___ .

Some notable ___E:towns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town)___ there include ___E:Prudhoe Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudhoe_Bay,_Alaska)___ , ___E:Utqiaġvik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utqia%C4%A1vik)___ , ___E:Kotzebue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kotzebue,_Alaska)___ , ___E:Nome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nome,_Alaska)___ and ___E:Galena U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galena,_Alaska)___ , although some of these are not in the ___E:Arctic Circle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_Circle)___ proper.

Most of these communities have no ___E:highways U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway)___ and can only be reached by ___E:aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft)___ or ___E:snowmobile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowmobile)___ in good ___E:weather U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather)___ .

Originally inhabited by various ___E:Alaska Native U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska_Native)___ groups living off hunting, whaling, or ___E:salmon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salmon)___ ___E:fishing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing)___ , modern settlement in Arctic Alaska was driven first by discoveries of ___E:gold U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold)___ and later on by the ___E:extraction of petroleum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraction_of_petroleum)___ .

The ___E:ecosystem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem)___ consists largely of ___E:tundra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tundra)___ covering ___E:mountain ranges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_range)___ and ___E:coastal plains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_plain)___ which are home to ___E:bears U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear)___ , ___E:wolves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaskan_tundra_wolf)___ , ___E:sheep U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep)___ , ___E:muskoxen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muskox)___ , ___E:caribou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porcupine_caribou)___ , and numerous ___E:species U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species)___ of ___E:birds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)___ , the north coast has been defined as the ___E:Arctic coastal tundra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_coastal_tundra)___ ecoregion.

Arctic Alaska is also the location of the ___E:Arctic National Wildlife Refuge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_National_Wildlife_Refuge)___ , ___E:Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gates_of_the_Arctic_National_Park_and_Preserve)___ , ___E:Kobuk Valley National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobuk_Valley_National_Park)___ and the ___E:National Petroleum Reserve–Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Petroleum_Reserve%E2%80%93Alaska)___ .
The Arctic experiences ___E:midnight sun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_sun)___ in the summer and ___E:polar night U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_night)___ in the winter.
Most of northern Alaska has an Arctic climate with long, extremely cold winters and short, cool summers.

The average temperatures during the summer months are only several degrees above freezing and the average temperatures during winter are as low as −20 to −30 °F (−29 to −34 °C), and can dip to −50 to −60 °F (−46 to −51 °C).
